risk_if_not_implemented: Without Configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for High-Risk Areas, Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) may operate with insecure, unauthorized or drifted configurations that expand the attack surface. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), System / Data Compromise (Technical Vector) (R-BC-4), System / Service Compromise (R-EX-7), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP)
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and monitoring of risk-based vulnerability management capabilities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Vulnerability & Patch Management Program (VPMP) (VPM-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for High-Risk Areas (CFG-05) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE)
compensating_control_2.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to:
(1) Identify unauthorized deviations from an approved secure baseline configuration; and
(2) Implement automated resiliency actions to remediate the unauthorized change.
compensating_control_2.justification: Integrity Assurance & Enforcement (IAE) (CFG-08.2) provides configuration hardening that compensates for the absence of Configure Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) for High-Risk Areas (CFG-05) by eliminating unnecessary services and enforcing secure settings to reduce inherent exposure. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
